source.headline: US Energy Chief Says Navy to Defend Hormuz Until Iran Backs Down

learning_v2.note: No context-aware v2 segment was used to materially alter confidence; current facts/context dominate.

predictions.mechanism: Persistent military protection of Hormuz transit signals prolonged geopolitical risk and supports safe-haven demand.
predictions.invalidation: A credible de-escalation agreement reduces military involvement and oil-flow risk.

predictions.mechanism: Persistently high oil and prolonged Hormuz risk raise European energy costs and risk premia.
predictions.invalidation: Oil drops sharply as transit normalizes or the conflict de-escalates.

predictions.mechanism: Higher energy-risk premia and supply uncertainty weigh on European cyclicals and margins.
predictions.invalidation: Brent falls materially and shipping conditions normalize.

predictions.mechanism: Elevated oil prices and geopolitical risk are a near-term headwind for broad European risk sentiment.
predictions.invalidation: Rapid de-escalation and lower crude prices.

predictions.mechanism: Japan is highly exposed to imported energy costs, while geopolitical risk can also strengthen the yen and pressure exporters.
predictions.invalidation: Oil reverses lower and yen pressure eases.
